south dakota.period1_limits: $50,000 per person / $100,000 per incident for death and bodily injury, $25,000 property damage
south dakota.period2_3_limits: $1,000,000 primary liability for death, bodily injury, and property damage while engaged in a prearranged ride (from acceptance of the ride request through drop-off)
south dakota.um_uim_note: Uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage is required in both periods as required by SDCL 58-11-9 and 58-11-9.4, at least at South Dakota's state minimum levels.
south dakota.who_pays_note: The driver, the TNC, or a combination of the two may provide the required primary coverage, which must expressly recognize that the driver is transporting riders for pay. A personal auto policy may exclude coverage while the driver is logged on or carrying a rider, so the TNC's policy is the one that responds in that case. If the app is off, only the driver's personal policy applies.
south dakota.tnc_statute: South Dakota Codified Laws chapter 32-40, Transportation Network Companies, especially SDCL 32-40-7 to 32-40-9 (2016 HB 1091)
south dakota.sol_note: The clock runs from the date the cause of action accrues, usually the crash date under SDCL 15-2-14(3); it is tolled for minors and persons of unsound mind under SDCL 15-2-22, and a claim against a public entity needs written notice within 180 days under SDCL 3-21-2.
south dakota.agency_name: South Dakota Department of Public Safety
south dakota.state_note: South Dakota's TNC law follows the standard national model exactly, and TNCs must register with the Department of Public Safety before operating in the state.
south dakota.sources: SDCL 32-40-7, 32-40-8, 32-40-9; SDCL 15-2-14(3); SDCL 58-11-9 and 58-11-9.4; South Dakota Department of Public Safety

tennessee.period1_limits: $50,000 per person / $100,000 per accident for bodily injury, $25,000 property damage
tennessee.period2_3_limits: $1,000,000 primary liability for death, bodily injury, and property damage from the moment the driver accepts a ride request until the ride is complete
tennessee.um_uim_note: Tenn. Code Ann. section 55-12-141 requires TNC coverage meeting Tennessee's uninsured motorist provisions (section 56-7-1201) in all three periods, but the TNC as named insured may affirmatively decline UM coverage, and the Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance has warned that at least one TNC opts out of UM coverage in Period 1, leaving a gap for drivers without their own UM coverage.
tennessee.who_pays_note: The driver or the TNC on the driver's behalf must maintain primary TNC insurance that recognizes the driver as a TNC driver. A Tennessee personal auto insurer may expressly exclude all coverage while the driver is acting as a TNC driver, and that exclusion removes any duty to defend or pay, so the TNC policy must carry the claim. If the app is off, only the driver's personal policy applies.
tennessee.tnc_statute: Tennessee Code Annotated section 55-12-141, Transportation Network Company Services Act, and Tenn. Code Ann. sections 56-7-3501 to 56-7-3504
tennessee.sol_note: Tennessee has the shortest deadline in this set: one year from accrual under Tenn. Code Ann. section 28-3-104(a)(1), with a discovery rule and tolling until age 18 for minors, and two years instead of one if criminal charges are brought over the same conduct.
tennessee.agency_name: Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance
tennessee.legal_aid_name: Legal Aid Society of Middle Tennessee and the Cumberlands
tennessee.state_note: Tennessee's one-year personal injury deadline is unusually short, and its UM opt-out creates a real Period 1 coverage gap the state regulator has publicly warned about; a 2025 law will also require TNC drivers to hold a state transportation network license from the Department of Commerce and Insurance starting January 1, 2026.
tennessee.sources: Tenn. Code Ann. section 55-12-141; Tenn. Code Ann. sections 56-7-3501 to 56-7-3504; Tenn. Code Ann. section 28-3-104(a)(1); Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance ridesharing notice

texas.period1_limits: $50,000 per person / $100,000 per incident for bodily injury or death, $25,000 property damage
texas.period2_3_limits: $1,000,000 total aggregate liability for death, bodily injury, and property damage for each incident while a rider is in the vehicle (Period 3); under HB 3520, for policies delivered, issued, or renewed on or after January 1, 2026, the en-route period with no rider in the vehicle (Period 2) is covered at the $50,000/$100,000/$25,000 level instead of $1,000,000
texas.um_uim_note: Uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage is required in both periods where required by Texas Insurance Code section 1952.101, and personal injury protection where required by section 1952.152; Texas UM/UIM is offered coverage that a named insured may reject in writing, so it is not automatic in every policy.
texas.who_pays_note: The driver or the TNC on the driver's behalf must maintain primary automobile insurance that allows the personal vehicle to be used to transport riders for pay, and the required coverage may come from the driver, the TNC, or both. A personal auto policy may exclude commercial use, in which case the TNC's primary coverage responds rather than the driver's personal insurer. If the app is off, only the driver's personal policy applies.
texas.tnc_statute: Texas Occupations Code chapter 2402, Transportation Network Companies (HB 100, 2017), and Texas Insurance Code chapter 1954, sections 1954.051 to 1954.053
texas.sol_note: Suit must be filed within two years after the cause of action accrues under Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code section 16.003, usually the crash date, with a narrow discovery rule and tolling for minors; a claim against a government entity needs written notice within six months under the Texas Tort Claims Act.
texas.agency_name: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation
texas.state_note: Texas is the notable outlier on Period 2: HB 3520 (2025) moved the en-route, no-rider-in-car period down from $1,000,000 to the $50,000/$100,000/$25,000 level for policies renewed on or after January 1, 2026, so the $1,000,000 tier now applies only once a rider is in the vehicle; Texas also regulates TNCs statewide through the Department of Licensing and Regulation, preempting local rules.
texas.sources: Tex. Ins. Code sections 1954.051, 1954.052, 1954.053; Tex. Occ. Code chapter 2402; Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code section 16.003; Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation TNC at a Glance

utah.period1_limits: $50,000 to any one individual / $100,000 to all individuals per occurrence for bodily injury, $30,000 property damage (note the higher $30,000 property damage figure, not $25,000)
utah.period2_3_limits: $1,000,000 per occurrence liability during a prearranged ride, from acceptance of the ride request through drop-off
utah.um_uim_note: Uninsured motorist coverage is required where required by Utah Code section 31A-22-305 and underinsured motorist coverage where required by section 31A-22-305.3, in both the waiting period and the prearranged ride; Utah also requires personal injury protection to the extent required by sections 31A-22-306 through 31A-22-309.
utah.who_pays_note: The TNC or the driver must maintain insurance on a primary basis that expressly acknowledges the driver is using the vehicle for a commercial purpose, and it may not wait for the driver's personal insurer to deny first. A personal auto policy need not cover TNC driving, and if the driver's required coverage has lapsed or is inadequate, the TNC must cover the claim from the first dollar. If the app is off, only the driver's personal policy applies.
utah.tnc_statute: Utah Code Title 13, chapter 51, Transportation Network Company Registration Act, especially Utah Code section 13-51-108
utah.sol_note: Utah gives four years for a personal injury claim under Utah Code section 78B-2-307(4), usually from the crash date, with tolling for minors until age 18; a claim against a government entity needs a written notice of claim within one year.
utah.agency_name: Utah Department of Commerce, Division of Consumer Protection
utah.state_note: Utah's Period 1 property damage minimum is $30,000 rather than the usual $25,000, Utah is a no-fault state so the first $3,000 in medical bills is paid by PIP and a tort claim for pain and suffering must clear the $3,000 medical-expense threshold in Utah Code section 31A-22-309, and a 2025 amendment (HB 220) added a cause of action against a TNC that fails to maintain proper insurance.
utah.sources: Utah Code section 13-51-108; Utah Code section 13-51-104; Utah Code section 78B-2-307(4); Utah Division of Consumer Protection TNC registration page

vermont.period1_limits: $50,000 per person / $100,000 per incident for death and bodily injury, $25,000 property damage, plus any other state-mandated coverage under 23 V.S.A. section 941
vermont.period2_3_limits: $1,000,000 primary liability for death, bodily injury, and property damage during a prearranged ride, plus at least $1,000,000 in uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage and $5,000 in medical payments coverage
vermont.um_uim_note: During a prearranged ride Vermont requires at least $1,000,000 in uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage under 23 V.S.A. section 750(b)(3), far above the usual state minimum; in Period 1 the statute requires any other state-mandated coverage under section 941, which includes Vermont's mandatory uninsured motorist coverage.
vermont.who_pays_note: The driver or the company on the driver's behalf must maintain primary automobile insurance that recognizes the driver is a company driver, and the coverage may come from the driver, the company, or both. If the driver's required coverage lapses or is inadequate, the company's coverage provides the required coverage, so an injured person is not left waiting on a personal insurer that excluded commercial use. If the app is off, only the driver's personal policy applies.
vermont.tnc_statute: 23 V.S.A. chapter 10, Transportation Network Companies, section 750 (2018 H.10)
vermont.sol_note: Actions for injuries to the person must be brought within three years under 12 V.S.A. section 512(4), and the cause of action is deemed to accrue on the date the injury is discovered; the clock is tolled for minors under 12 V.S.A. section 551.
vermont.state_note: Vermont is the strongest UM/UIM state in this set: the prearranged-ride period requires $1,000,000 in UM/UIM coverage plus $5,000 in medical payments coverage, and the statute requires the company to disclose precise log-on and log-off times for the 12 hours before and after a crash during a coverage investigation.
vermont.sources: 23 V.S.A. section 750; 12 V.S.A. section 512(4); Vermont Department of Motor Vehicles

virginia.period1_limits: $50,000 per person / $100,000 per incident for death and bodily injury, $25,000 property damage
virginia.period2_3_limits: $1,000,000 primary liability for death, bodily injury, and property damage from the moment the driver accepts a prearranged ride request until the ride is complete or the transaction is closed, whichever is later
virginia.um_uim_note: Uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage is required in both periods as required by Va. Code section 38.2-2206; Virginia UM/UIM is mandatory coverage, and since January 1, 2025 the state's minimum liability limits are $50,000/$100,000/$25,000.
virginia.who_pays_note: The TNC or the TNC partner must keep TNC insurance in force at all times during operation of the vehicle, and the TNC coverage is primary in both periods. A personal auto policy may exclude driving for pay, so the TNC's primary policy is the one that pays while the driver is logged on or carrying a rider. If the app is off, only the driver's personal policy applies.
virginia.tnc_statute: Code of Virginia sections 46.2-2099.48 to 46.2-2099.56, especially section 46.2-2099.52, TNC insurance
virginia.sol_note: Every action for personal injuries must be brought within two years after the cause of action accrues under Va. Code section 8.01-243(A), usually the crash date; the clock is tolled for minors and for legal disability, and a claim against a city or county needs written notice within six months while a claim against the state needs notice within one year.
virginia.state_note: Virginia's TNC coverage is expressly primary in both periods, and Virginia requires TNCs to obtain a certificate of fitness from the DMV before operating; the state's base auto minimums also rose to $50,000/$100,000/$25,000 for policies issued or renewed on or after January 1, 2025, so Period 1 now matches the ordinary state minimum.
virginia.sources: Va. Code section 46.2-2099.52; Va. Code section 8.01-243(A); Va. Code section 38.2-2206; Virginia Department of Motor Vehicles TNC FAQ

washington.period1_limits: $50,000 per person / $100,000 per accident for bodily injury, $30,000 property damage (note the higher $30,000 property damage figure, not $25,000)
washington.period2_3_limits: $1,000,000 combined single limit liability for death, personal injury, and property damage during a prearranged ride
washington.um_uim_note: In Period 1, underinsured motorist coverage is required to the extent required by RCW 48.22.030, plus personal injury protection to the extent required by RCW 48.22.085 and 48.22.095; during a prearranged ride the statute requires underinsured motorist coverage of $100,000 per person and $300,000 per accident from the moment a passenger enters the vehicle until the passenger exits, plus PIP as required by law.
washington.who_pays_note: Every personal vehicle used for TNC services must be covered by a primary automobile insurance policy that specifically covers TNC services, secured by the TNC for every vehicle unless the driver has approved coverage. If the driver's policy does not provide coverage for any reason, including a lapse, the TNC must provide the required coverage beginning with the first dollar of the claim. If the app is off, only the driver's personal policy applies.
washington.tnc_statute: Revised Code of Washington chapter 46.72B, Transportation Network Companies, especially RCW 46.72B.180 (insurance), and RCW chapter 48.177, Commercial Transportation Services
washington.sol_note: An action for injury to the person must be commenced within three years under RCW 4.16.080(2), usually from the crash date, with a discovery rule for injuries discovered later and tolling for minors and legal disability under RCW 4.16.190; a claim against the state or a local government needs a claim form first, then a 60-day wait before suit.
washington.state_note: Washington's Period 1 property damage minimum is $30,000 rather than $25,000, its prearranged-ride UIM figure is a specific $100,000/$300,000 for the passenger-occupied period, and a TNC must obtain an annual $5,000 permit from the Department of Licensing.
washington.sources: RCW 46.72B.180; RCW 4.16.080(2); RCW 48.22.030; Washington State Department of Licensing TNC license page

west virginia.period1_limits: $50,000 per person / $100,000 per incident for death and bodily injury, $25,000 property damage
west virginia.period2_3_limits: $1,000,000 primary liability for death, bodily injury, and property damage while engaged in a prearranged ride
west virginia.um_uim_note: Uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage is required in both periods as required by W. Va. Code section 33-6-31, which sets West Virginia's mandatory uninsured motorist coverage.
west virginia.who_pays_note: The driver or the TNC on the driver's behalf must maintain primary automobile insurance that recognizes the driver is a TNC driver, and the TNC's coverage does not depend on the personal insurer first denying a claim. If the driver's insurance has lapsed or does not provide the required coverage, the TNC's insurance provides it beginning with the first dollar of the claim and has the duty to defend. If the app is off, only the driver's personal policy applies.
west virginia.tnc_statute: West Virginia Code chapter 17, article 29, Transportation Network Companies, sections 17-29-1 to 17-29-19, especially section 17-29-8
west virginia.sol_note: A personal injury action must be brought within two years after the right to bring it accrues under W. Va. Code section 55-2-12(b), usually the crash date, with a discovery rule for injuries that could not reasonably have been discovered and tolling for minors and legal disability.
west virginia.agency_name: West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles
west virginia.state_note: West Virginia expressly makes TNC coverage independent of any personal-insurer denial and first-dollar where the driver's coverage lapses, and a TNC may not operate in the state without a $1,000 annual permit from the Division of Motor Vehicles under section 17-29-3.
west virginia.sources: W. Va. Code section 17-29-8; W. Va. Code section 17-29-3; W. Va. Code section 55-2-12(b); W. Va. Code section 33-6-31; West Virginia Division of Motor Vehicles

wisconsin.period1_limits: $50,000 per person / $100,000 per incident for death and bodily injury, $25,000 property damage
wisconsin.period2_3_limits: $1,000,000 primary liability for death, bodily injury, and property damage while engaged in transportation network services (from acceptance of the ride request through drop-off)
wisconsin.um_uim_note: Primary uninsured motorist coverage is required in both periods in accordance with Wis. Stat. section 632.32(4)(a)1; Wisconsin requires uninsured motorist coverage of at least $25,000 per person and $50,000 per accident, and the TNC policy must provide it on a primary basis.
wisconsin.who_pays_note: The participating driver or the TNC on the driver's behalf must maintain primary automobile insurance that recognizes the driver is a participating driver, and the coverage may come from the driver, the TNC, or both. A Wisconsin personal auto insurer may exclude all coverage while the driver is logged on or engaged in TNC services, and if the driver's coverage lapses or is inadequate, the TNC's insurance provides the required coverage beginning with the first dollar and has the duty to defend. If the app is off, only the driver's personal policy applies.
wisconsin.tnc_statute: Wisconsin Statutes sections 440.40 to 440.49, Transportation Network Companies, especially Wis. Stat. section 440.48 (insurance) and section 440.415 (licensure)
wisconsin.sol_note: An action for injuries to the person, including one arising from a motor vehicle accident, must be commenced within three years under Wis. Stat. section 893.54(1m)(a), with a discovery rule that starts the clock when the plaintiff has enough evidence that a wrong was committed by an identified person, and tolling for minors; note that a wrongful death claim from a motor vehicle accident is only two years under section 893.54(2m).
wisconsin.agency_name: Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services
wisconsin.state_note: Wisconsin licenses TNCs through the Department of Safety and Professional Services rather than a DMV or utilities commission, and Legal Action of Wisconsin merged with Judicare Legal Aid on January 1, 2026 to become one statewide legal aid firm under the Legal Action name.
wisconsin.sources: Wis. Stat. section 440.48; Wis. Stat. section 440.415; Wis. Stat. section 893.54(1m)(a); Wis. Stat. section 632.32(4)(a)1; Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services TNC page

wyoming.period1_limits: $50,000 per person / $100,000 per incident for death and bodily injury, $25,000 property damage
wyoming.period2_3_limits: $1,000,000 primary liability for death, bodily injury, and property damage while engaged in a prearranged ride (from acceptance of the ride request through drop-off)
wyoming.um_uim_note: Uninsured motorist coverage is required in both periods as required by Wyo. Stat. section 31-10-101; Wyoming requires uninsured motorist coverage of at least $25,000 per person and $50,000 per accident.
wyoming.who_pays_note: The driver or the TNC on the driver's behalf must maintain a motor vehicle liability policy that recognizes the driver is a TNC driver, and the requirement may be met by the driver, the TNC, or both. Coverage under a TNC policy does not depend on the personal insurer first denying a claim, and if the driver's insurance has lapsed or is inadequate, the TNC's insurance provides the required coverage beginning with the first dollar and its insurer has the duty to defend. If the app is off, only the driver's personal policy applies.
wyoming.tnc_statute: Wyoming Statutes sections 31-20-101 to 31-20-111, Transportation Network Companies, especially Wyo. Stat. section 31-20-107 (2017 HB 80)
wyoming.sol_note: A personal injury action must be brought within four years after the cause of action accrues under Wyo. Stat. section 1-3-105(a)(iv)(C), usually the crash date, with a discovery rule for injuries discovered later and tolling for minors until age 18; a claim against a government entity needs a notice of claim within one year under the Wyoming Governmental Claims Act.
wyoming.agency_name: No single TNC regulator in Wyoming — the Wyoming Department of Insurance oversees the insurance requirements and the Wyoming Department of Transportation handles vehicle registration; the statute bars any state or local entity from requiring a TNC license to operate
wyoming.state_note: Wyoming is the only state in this set with no TNC permit or license at all: section 31-20-111 bars any municipality or state entity from requiring a TNC or driver to obtain a license to operate, and since July 1, 2025 drivers must show Wyoming motor vehicle registration for the vehicle used (2025 HB 77).
wyoming.sources: Wyo. Stat. section 31-20-107; Wyo. Stat. section 31-20-108; Wyo. Stat. section 1-3-105(a)(iv)(C); Wyo. Stat. section 31-10-101
